newsitem.title: USA: Levitz debt gains on eve of Dec sales report.
newsitem.headline: Levitz debt gains on eve of Dec sales report.

text.p: Levitz Furniture Inc debt gained more than three points on Monday prior to the release of the company's same-store sales figure for December, corporate bond high-yield traders said.
Despite the absence of any fresh news, Levitz's 9.625 percent notes due 2003 gained over three points on Monday to trade at 65-3/4 bid, 66-1/4 offer, traders said.
Traders were at a loss for an explanation concerning the improvement of the debt. Some speculated the move was tied to Tuesday's release of the company's December sales figures.
Gary Miller, Levitz's assistant treasurer declined to comment on any expectations for the December sales report.

When asked about the substantial 3-3/4 point gain in the company's debt on Monday, Miller responded: "I can only speculate that someone else is speculating on it. We have put nothing out and will have nothing out until tomorrow."
In November, Levitz reported a 13.0 percent increase in same-store sales, the first monthly gain following a string of negative monthly reports for the 1996 year.
Last January, Levitz posted its biggest monthly decline for the year reporting a 16.9 percent drop in same-store sales.
